 Sophie Cunningham Says Indiana Fever Had Just 200 Fans Before Caitlin Clark Arrived
 Sophie Cunningham told Theo Von that Indiana went from a sleepy stop to “people’s Super Bowl,” just as her own Fever future becomes uncertain.
 Chirag Radhyan 
 Oct 29, 2026 
 5 Min Read 
 Share 
 Sophie Cunnigham, Caitlin Clark 
 The Indiana Fever have been the WNBA’s most-watched franchise since they drafted Caitlin Clark. This season, that fame climbed even higher, even though the team did not make a deep playoff run.
 Sophie Cunningham just explained how wild that swing has been. Speaking with Theo Von on the ‘This Past Weekend’ podcast, the Fever guard looked back at what Indiana was like when she entered the league.
 Von asked how much things changed when the draft class that included Caitlin Clark, Angel Reese, and Cameron Brink arrived, with Paige Bueckers coming a year later. Cunningham said the change was night and day, and that it came immediately.
 Cunningham was drafted by the Phoenix Mercury in 2019, where Diana Taurasi helped keep arenas sold out. Packed crowds were nothing new to her.
 Indiana was the contrast. She said the Fever had only about 200 fans back then, and players wanted out as soon as the game ended.
 That has flipped completely.
 “ When I got drafted, Indiana, I think they only had like 200 fans ,” Cunningham said . “ Like, it was a nap town. People went there to catch up on sleep. You played a game and you wanted to get out. Now, that’s the place you want to play. That’s like people’s Super Bowl… Now, every arena’s like that. ”
 The change goes past the crowds, she said. Since that class arrived, teams now have private flights and security. Some teams are still working to reach that level, she added, but she said the Fever are at the highest level you can get.
 A team that once struggled to draw a crowd is now the league’s most-watched. Even a joke about napping hits harder when you know who fills the building today.
 Indiana’s roots run deeper than the Clark era. The Fever won a championship in 2012 and enjoyed decent success in the Tamika Catchings years. Things slid after 2016, and the two seasons before Clark arrived were arguably the worst in franchise history.
 The 2024 draft changed that path. League popularity is now at an all-time high, and the Fever sit at the center of it. There is still plenty of growing left to do.
 Fame at that level carries a cost, and Cunningham addressed it on the same podcast. She said more TV exposure brings more fans, but it also brings “a lot of stalkers,” and she has dealt with them too. She said players want to feel secure.
 She also claimed, while noting she needed to check if she could say it, that the FBI is watching roughly 20 people on her behalf.
 What The Front Office Shake-Up Means For Sophie Cunningham’s Fever Future
 Indiana’s season ended in the first round, with a 94-83 loss to the Las Vegas Aces in Game 3. The front office changes followed soon after.
 Cunningham is an unrestricted free agent, and the Fever recently fired general manager Amber Cox . Team president Kelly Krauskopf also stepped down.
 Those two ran the franchise when Cunningham arrived in a four-team trade and when she re-signed in April. She stayed gracious about their exits.
 “ I couldn’t love them more ,” Cunningham said.
 Cox spoke highly of Cunningham too. The guard ranked seventh in the WNBA in three-point shooting at 41.9 percent this season, and third in points per scoring attempt at 1.31. Cox also praised her as a solid leader in the locker room.
 Those marks help explain why Indiana would want to keep her. The new front office now inherits that call.
 For now, Cunningham says she is embracing where her feet are planted, with a business project set to start in January. That sounds like a player at peace with any outcome, but the Fever do not have that luxury. The Fever now need new leadership to guide a franchise that went from a sleepy stop to the league’s biggest stage.
